tasks.short: Analyze stock and till totals for theft or fraud trends

steps.what: Pull stock units and till totals
Sign the monthly exception thresholds
Run exception queries on those totals
Draft a theft and fraud trend note

loop.input: exception rows and the note template
loop.output: trend note that cites store and week only
loop.check: Every figure equals a row on the exception list and no employee name appears
loop.stop: One draft, then drop any sentence with no store id
loop.why_not_simpler: Saying whether a pattern is theft or a recording error is not a fixed lookup

steps.what: Decide which trends to brief
File the signed trend note

tasks.design: Stock units and till totals land on a {BI} view by store and week, with no employee field. The loss prevention manager signs the exception thresholds, a fixed query on the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP} marks the rows outside them, and a bounded note in {DOCS} may cite only those rows. The manager decides which trends are briefed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Totals lived in separate extracts and a spreadsheet, so a note could not show which store-week it used.
tasks.enabler_now: Stock and till exports can share a store id and a week, which is enough for a fixed threshold.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing which pattern matters, and whether it is theft, fraud or a recording error, is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides which trends are worth a briefing and which rows are noise.

ambition.what: Sign a trend note every month from stock and till exceptions, not only after a bad shrink result

tasks.altitude: Less time rebuilding extracts, more time on the rows that fail a threshold. The manager can refuse a note that cites a figure that is not on the list.

reach.task: Explain a store-week the trend note marked
reach.learn: Which thresholds are signed and which stores were briefed

evidence.claim: In a mid-size retailer this task is a periodic extract of stock and till totals, and the hard part is which pattern is worth a briefing.
Digest [S8] says a new incident register increased reports sharply, and that is more reporting, not fewer incidents, so a rise in flagged rows is not by itself a new theft wave.
Digest [S9] says GDPR article 22 does not allow a solely automated decision about a person, so a till total is not turned into an action about an employee.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. The task ends when a signed trend note is filed. An investigation of a named person is a later task and is not counted as saved.

Input contract: store id, week, stock units expected, stock units counted, till total, tender, refund total. Producer is the stock and till export. No employee id. If a row lacks store id or week, it stays on a manual list. If the export contains an employee id, that column is dropped and not used.
Native dashboard filters and the existing export are configured before custom code. The meeting share in the prior is only the briefing.
unknowns: Whether the stock export and the till export share a store id.
Who may sign thresholds when the manager is absent.
Whether a works council would treat a later employee cut of this file as staff monitoring.
research_questions: What share of store-weeks lack a stock count or a till total?
How often does a flagged row turn out to be a recording error?

already_counted.description: Manager edits a trend sentence that the check did not catch
Manager time in the briefing stays inside the decision

incremental.description: Revise threshold fields when a new tender or stock type appears
Store managers correct a store id the export rejected

approvals.approved_version: exception thresholds signed for this month
trend note signed in this briefing

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many rows lack a store id, so the query rarely runs and the manager still builds the extract by hand. The high case assumes clean totals but every briefing is still a human decision. Actions about a named employee are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct store, safety, maintenance and article-surveillance audits

steps.what: Direct safety and store audit types
Issue the signed audit checklists
Complete maintenance and surveillance audits
Classify audit notes against checklist items

loop.input: fail notes and checklist item ids
loop.output: each note tagged to one item id or unmatched
loop.check: Every tag is an item id on that store's checklist
loop.stop: One pass, then unmatched notes wait for the manager
loop.why_not_simpler: A free-text note does not map to an item by a fixed table

steps.what: Decide which failed audits stay open
File the signed audit pack

tasks.design: The loss prevention manager signs which audit types are due on a {WORKFLOW} form: target store, maintenance, safety, or article surveillance. Checklists in {DOCS} go only to those stores. Stores file pass or fail plus a note, a bounded pass classifies the note against checklist items, and the manager decides which fails stay open. The walk stays in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Audit types, due stores and fail notes were spread across mail and paper sheets, so a cycle could not be issued from one signed choice.
tasks.enabler_now: A checklist item id and a store id can travel with the result, which is enough to file and to flag a failed item.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a repeated fail is poor upkeep or a real loss risk is still the manager's call, and the walk cannot be done from a desk.
tasks.human_edge: The manager chooses the audit mix and decides which failed items stay open.

ambition.what: Close or reopen failed audit items every cycle, not only at the yearly review

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time chasing missing sheets and keeps the right to drop an audit type or hold a fail open. Store walks do not move.

reach.task: Complete the checklist the program named for that store
reach.learn: Which audit types are due and which fails the manager left open

evidence.claim: Digest [S2] describes GRC modules for compliance, audit, incident and regulatory monitoring, which can hold an audit cycle and its results for a person to close.
Digest [S12] says works council consent is needed before staff monitoring, so an audit that watches how staff work needs that consent first.
In a mid-size retailer the manager directs the audit cycle, and store staff still walk the floor for safety, maintenance and article-surveillance checks.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. The task ends when the signed audit pack for the cycle is filed. Doing the walk is the store's time.

Input contract: audit type, store id, checklist item id, pass or fail, note, audit date, auditor role. Audit type is one of target store, maintenance, safety, article surveillance. Producer is the store manager. A sheet with no store id or no item id is keyed later and marked manual.

Article surveillance here means an in-person check of overt tags and pedestals, not a camera program and not a score of staff. Native workflow checklists are configured before custom code. If the walk watches staff at work, it waits for works council consent.
unknowns: Whether article-surveillance checks are done by store staff or by a specialist.
Which fails are allowed to stay open past one cycle.
Whether consent for staff observation is already on file.
research_questions: What share of due audits arrive with no checklist item id?
How many failed items are still open from the previous cycle?

already_counted.description: Manager corrects unmatched audit notes before the decision
Manager time on which fails stay open

incremental.description: Update checklist items when a new audit type or fixture appears
Stores resubmit sheets rejected for a missing item id

approvals.approved_version: audit cycle signed for this period
fail decision signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most results still arrive as paper, so classification rarely runs and the manager still chases sheets. The high case assumes typed results but every open fail and every choice of audit type stays with the manager. The store walk is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Work with law enforcement on external theft or fraud cases

steps.what: Ask for the external case facts
Open the external theft case
Draft the fact pack from logged fields

loop.input: logged case fields and the pack template
loop.output: pack that cites only logged fields
loop.check: Every value equals the register and every name was already on the case
loop.stop: One draft; leave a blank where the register is empty and do not invent a name
loop.why_not_simpler: The narrative of what the agency should do is not a field on the register

steps.what: Investigate the case with law enforcement
Decide what the agency may receive
Send the signed fact pack

tasks.design: A case already on the {WORKFLOW} register supplies store, date, goods, value and any name a person has already recorded. A bounded pack in {DOCS} may cite only those fields. The loss prevention manager meets law enforcement, decides what may be shared, and only that signed pack is sent. The investigation and any interview stay a meeting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts for an external case were copied from mail and notebooks, so a pack could not be tied to one case id.
tasks.enabler_now: The incident register can export a case id and the fields already logged, which is enough to draft a pack without adding new facts.
tasks.still_hard: What happened, and what an agency should receive, is still decided in the meeting with the officer.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides what leaves the company and what stays unshared.

ambition.what: Decide within the week what may be shared with the agency, instead of leaving the pack in mail

tasks.altitude: Preparation of the pack takes less rewriting. The meeting and the decision about what an agency may see do not move.

reach.task: Use the signed fact pack in the external case
reach.learn: Which facts the manager has agreed to share and which fields were left blank

evidence.claim: Digest [S3] says incident reports are forwarded to the person in charge, so a case pack waits for the manager rather than going out on its own.
Digest [S9] says GDPR article 22 does not allow a solely automated decision about a person, and sharing a case about someone is such a decision.
Digest [S15] says a model-drafted paid report cited sources that did not exist, so a person stays on anything sent to an agency.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. The task runs from an open external case to a signed pack sent or a decision not to share. Interviews stay in the meeting and are not scripted here.

Input contract: case id, store id, date, goods description, goods value, name if a person already recorded one, agency, officer name. Producer is the incident register. Empty fields stay blank. The draft must not invent a name, a time or a value.
Native register export and mail are configured before custom code. The meeting prior is right for this task: the investigation itself stays in person.
unknowns: Which agency is the usual contact for this firm.
Whether a recording already kept for the incident may be listed, and who may release it.
Who may sign a share decision when the manager is absent.
research_questions: What share of external cases have a complete goods value on the register?
How often does the manager refuse to share a field the agency asked for?

already_counted.description: Manager corrects a pack line before the meeting
Meeting time with the officer stays with the manager

incremental.description: Keep the pack template aligned with the fields the register actually stores
Officers send a follow-up when a shared field was blank

approvals.approved_version: share decision signed for this case id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes case facts stay in notebooks, so the pack is still typed by hand and the meeting is unchanged. The high case assumes a clean register but every share decision and the investigation meeting stay with the manager. Interview time is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Coordinate investigations of organized theft and fraud groups

steps.what: Log the theft incident with a method code
Sign match rules with no person key
Match open cases on goods and dates
Decide if cases are one organized group
Coordinate the organized group investigation
Draft fraud investigations status notes

loop.input: signed link and logged incident fields
loop.output: status note citing incident ids only
loop.check: Every incident id in the note is on the signed group link
loop.stop: One draft; drop any sentence with no incident id and add no name
loop.why_not_simpler: What the meeting concluded is not a fixed field

steps.what: Sign the investigation status note
File the signed investigation status

tasks.design: Stores log a theft incident on the {WORKFLOW} register with store, date, goods and a method code a person already chose. A signed rule matches open cases on those fields only, never on a name. The loss prevention manager decides which matches are one organized group, runs the coordination meeting, and signs the status note in {DOCS}. Interviews stay in that meeting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Links between cases were remembered in meetings, so two stores could not see whether their incidents had been joined.
tasks.enabler_now: Incidents can share goods type, store and date, which is enough for a fixed match the manager can accept or reject.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding that separate incidents are one group, and running that investigation, is still a people judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The manager accepts or rejects a suggested link and leads the coordination meeting.

ambition.what: Accept or reject a suggested case link within the week, instead of waiting for the next regional meeting

tasks.altitude: Suggested links are visible sooner. The manager still decides the group and still runs the investigation meeting. Nothing about interviewing a person moves.

reach.task: Log the incident fields the match is allowed to use
reach.learn: Which of their incidents were joined to a group and which links the manager rejected

evidence.claim: Digest [S3] says incident reports are forwarded to the person in charge, so a suggested link is not itself a decision that cases form one group.
Digest [S8] says a new incident register increased reports sharply, and that is more reporting, not fewer incidents, so a spike in logs is not by itself a new group.
Digest [S9] says GDPR article 22 does not allow a solely automated decision about a person, so a name is not a match key and is not an outcome of the rule.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. The task ends when a signed status for the group investigation is filed. Interviews are person_does inside the coordination meeting and are not designed here.

Input contract: incident id, store id, date, goods type, method code, value. Producer is the store manager on the register. Match rules the manager signs may use only goods type, store and date window. A name is never a match key. Rows with no goods type or no date stay unmatched.
Native register filters are configured before custom code. A rise in logged incidents is not treated as proof of a new group.
unknowns: Who is allowed to set the method code on an incident.
How wide a date window the manager will sign.
Whether group status is shared with an agency or kept internal.
research_questions: What share of incidents have goods type and date filled?
How often does the manager reject a suggested link?

already_counted.description: Manager rejects weak links inside the group decision
Coordination meeting time stays with the manager

incremental.description: Revise the allowed match fields when goods categories change
Stores correct a goods type the match could not read

approvals.approved_version: match rules signed for this period
group link decision for these incident ids
investigation status signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes method and goods are free text, so the match rarely runs and coordination stays a meeting. The high case assumes coded incidents but every group decision, the meeting and the status sign-off stay with the manager. Interview time is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week moves from rebuilding theft and fraud packs to signing which trends, audit fails and case links are real, while police meetings and interviews stay in the room.
reach: Store managers receive the signed audit pack and the failed items still open.
A security manager can read which external theft cases already have a signed fact pack.
skills_to_grow: State an exception as stock units and till totals, with no employee field.
Keep a police meeting as the place an external case is decided.
Separate a suggested case link from the decision that two cases are one group.
role.ambitious_version: Each month ends with a signed trend note from stock and till exceptions, and every open organized-group case has an owner and a next date.
